beats.1: An entity is a distinguishable real-world object. Attributes describe entities. A relationship represents an association between entities.
beats.2: Simple: cannot be meaningfully divided. Composite: has components. Single-valued: one value. Multivalued: several values. Derived: calculated from other data. Key attribute: uniquely identifies an entity.
beats.3: Super key uniquely identifies. Candidate key is a minimal super key. Primary key is the chosen candidate key. Alternate key is an unchosen candidate key. Foreign key references a key in another relation.
beats.4: Cardinality can be 1:1, 1:N or M:N. Total participation is mandatory; partial participation is optional.
beats.5: For an M:N relationship, create a separate relation containing the primary keys of both entities, usually as a composite primary key. Relationship attributes such as EnrollmentDate live there too.
beats.6: Relation = table, tuple = row, attribute = column, domain = permitted values, degree = number of attributes, cardinality = number of tuples.
beats.7: Strong entity → relation. Composite attribute → store components. Multivalued attribute → separate relation. 1:1 → FK on one side, preferably total participation side. 1:N → 1-side key goes into N-side. M:N → separate relation. Weak entity → owner key + partial key.
